summary_table.content: - Narrowest Points: External urethral meatus is narrowest overall (rigid); membranous urethra is narrowest and least dilatable inside. • Widest Points: Prostatic urethra (most dilatable) and Fossa Navicularis in glans penis. • Posterior Wall Features: Urethral crest -> expands into Colliculus Seminalis (Verumontanum). • Prostatic Utricle: Blind cul-de-sac at center of verumontanum; homologue of female Uterus and Vagina. • Ejaculatory Ducts: Open on either side of the prostatic utricle. • Prostatic Sinuses: Grooves on sides of crest receiving 15-20 ducts of the prostatic gland. • BPH vs Cancer: BPH affects periurethral Transition Zone (early obstruction); Cancer affects Peripheral Zone (posterior, no early obstruction). • Membranous Urethra: Traverses Deep Perineal Pouch; surrounded by striated External Urethral Sphincter (Pudendal nerve S2-S4).
• Cowper's (Bulbourethral) Glands: Lie in deep perineal pouch; ducts pierce perineal membrane to open into bulbous spongy urethra.

• Spongy Urethra: Enclosed in Corpus Spongiosum. Has 2 dilatations: Intrabulbar fossa & Navicular fossa (roof valve of Guérin). • Curvatures: Posterior/Subpubic (fixed, concave upwards); Anterior/Prepubic (obliterated by elevating flaccid penis). • Bulbous Spongy Rupture (Straddle Injury): Urine extravasates into Superficial Perineal Pouch (beneath Colles' fascia) → passes into

Scrotum, Penis, and Anterior Abdominal Wall (deep to Scarpa's fascia). Cannot enter thighs (Scarpa fuses with Fascia Lata 1 fingerbreadth below inguinal lig) or anal triangle (Colles fuses with posterior perineal membrane). • Membranous Rupture (Pelvic Fracture): Urine extravasates into Deep Perineal Pouch & Retropubic Space of Retzius (extraperitoneal pelvis). Produces 'High-Riding / Floating' prostate on rectal exam. • Length: 4 cm (1.5 inches). Runs anteroinferiorly embedded in anterior vaginal wall.

• External Meatus: Located in vaginal vestibule, ~2.5 cm posterior to clitoris, immediately anterior to vaginal orifice. • Skene's (Paraurethral) Glands: Open adjacent to external meatus; homologue of male prostate gland. • Clinical Significance: Short straight course predisposes females to high rate of ascending bacterial UTIs. • Hypospadias: Ventral urethral opening due to failure of fusion of urogenital (urethral) folds.

questions.text: The total anatomical length of the adult male urethra from the internal to the external meatus is approximately:
questions.explanation:
**Prostatic Urethra & Crest**: - Narrowest Points: External urethral meatus is narrowest overall (rigid); membranous urethra is narrowest and least dilatable inside. • Widest Points: Prostatic urethra (most dilatable) and Fossa Navicularis in glans penis. • Posterior Wall Features: Urethral crest -> expands into Colliculus Seminalis (Verumontanum). • Prostatic Utricle: Blind cul-de-sac at center of verumontanum; homologue of female Uterus and Vagina. • Ejaculatory Ducts: Open on either side of the prostatic utricle. • Prostatic Sinuses: Grooves on sides of crest receiving 15-20 ducts of the prostatic gland. • BPH vs Cancer: BPH affects periurethral Transition Zone (early obstruction); Cancer affects Peripheral Zone (posterior, no early obstruction). • Membranous Urethra: Traverses Deep Perineal Pouch; surrounded by striated External Urethral Sphincter (Pudendal nerve S2-S4).

**Membranous & Spongy**: • Cowper's (Bulbourethral) Glands: Lie in deep perineal pouch; ducts pierce perineal membrane to open into bulbous spongy urethra.

**Prostatic Urethra & Crest**: - Narrowest Points: External urethral meatus is narrowest overall (rigid); membranous urethra is narrowest and least dilatable inside. • Widest Points: Prostatic urethra (most dilatable) and Fossa Navicularis in glans penis. • Posterior Wall Features: Urethral crest -> expands into Colliculus Seminalis (Verumontanum). • Prostatic Utricle: Blind cul-de-sac at center of verumontanum; homologue of female Uterus and Vagina. • Ejaculatory Ducts: Open on either side of the prostatic utricle. • Prostatic Sinuses: Grooves on sides of crest receiving 15-20 ducts of the prostatic gland. • BPH vs Cancer: BPH affects periurethral Transition Zone (early obstruction); Cancer affects Peripheral Zone (posterior, no early obstruction). • Membranous Urethra: Traverses Deep Perineal Pouch; surrounded by striated External Urethral Sphincter (Pudendal nerve S2-S4).

**Membranous & Spongy**: • Cowper's (Bulbourethral) Glands: Lie in deep perineal pouch; ducts pierce perineal membrane to open into bulbous spongy urethra.

**Membranous & Spongy**: • Cowper's (Bulbourethral) Glands: Lie in deep perineal pouch; ducts pierce perineal membrane to open into bulbous spongy urethra.
